answer.narrative: Nvidia's revenue jumped from $26.97 billion to $60.92 billion in fiscal 2024, a 125.9% increase [F3]. This surge was driven by demand that outstripped supply, which allowed the company to expand its gross margin from 56.9% to 72.7% [F5]. Sales clearly ran ahead of inventory, which grew only 2.4% despite the massive revenue leap [F8]. Operating leverage further amplified the result, with operating income surging 680.6% compared to the revenue gain [F11]. While semiconductor prices were roughly flat year-over-year, the revenue move was driven by volume or mix rather than industry-wide pricing shifts [F19]. The strongest counter-evidence is that inventory levels barely budged, proving the growth was demand-led rather than supply-driven [F8].
